claims.text: Elevated-temperature oxidation resistance in HEAs is caused by a synergy between high configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion.
High configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion enable selective oxidation of protective elements such as Al or Cr.
Selective oxidation of Al, Cr, or related elements can produce a dense, adherent mixed-oxide layer on an HEA.
A dense protective oxide layer can self-limit further oxidation.
Oxidation at approximately 800–1100 °C can form an oxide film enriched in Al2O3, Cr-rich oxides, or related protective oxides.
High configurational entropy promotes sluggish diffusion of alloying elements in HEAs.
Limited elemental mobility permits controlled preferential oxidation.
Preferential oxidation is governed by the oxide-forming tendencies, thermodynamics, and redox behavior of the constituent elements.
The presence of several elements stabilizes a mixed oxide scale.
The resulting protective scale resists oxygen ingress.
The proposed protective scale prevents formation of non-protective, rapidly growing oxide phases.
Relative to conventional alloys with similar constituents but lower configurational entropy, HEAs will form thinner, more uniform, and more adherent oxide layers.
Relative to the conventional-alloy baseline, HEAs will oxidize more slowly, show reduced mass gain, and exhibit more favorable oxide phase compositions.
Conventional alloys with similar primary elements but lower configurational entropy typically develop thicker and less protective oxide scales.
The mechanism is effective only when the HEA contains elements capable of forming stable protective oxides.
HEAs lacking effective protective-oxide formers, or dominated by volatile oxides, may not exhibit the proposed behavior.
Oxide-scale composition and structure vary with alloy chemistry and environmental conditions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes Al or Cr as minor protective elements, while the equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi example would contain approximately 20 at.% of each and therefore does not treat Al or Cr as minor constituents.
